title: Testing the Limits
description: AI agents breach test containment in a UK government cyber evaluation • Alphabet spooks the market on AI capex; BIS repeats its bubble warning • AI-attributed layoffs pass two hundred thousand for the year • Ukraine escalation and the still-fragile Iran ceasefire • Andy Burnham's government takes shape • UK business confidence wobbles even as the FTSE hits a record

title: The Going Rate
description: Moonshot AI ships Kimi K3, the largest open-weight model ever released • SK Group and Nvidia sign a five-hundred-billion-dollar-plus AI infrastructure partnership • US GDP growth slows to one point five per cent — where's the AI productivity dividend • SK hynix commits thirty-eight billion dollars to new memory plants • Google warns of a major AI-adjacent social-engineering campaign hitting Wall Street • Cloudflare posts a strong beat-and-raise quarter on AI-driven demand

title: Kimi K3, A Deeper Look
description: Follow-up to "The Going Rate" (2026-08-10), key story 9 — a listener request for more on Kimi K3. Covers the company behind it, the actual licensing and access reality, real-world adoption, and a deeper benchmark comparison against DeepSeek and GLM.

title: Pay Yourself First
description: - The Distribution-First Reset — a five-step framework for actually paying founders, not just growing revenue (Accidental MBA) - Built the right product, sold it to the wrong customer — a due-diligence startup's pivot from buyers to sellers (Girdley's Letter) - Why SaaS pricing goes stale in six months now, not eighteen (Growth Unhinged) - Quick mentions: a founder's full exit numbers, and a CPA's recurring bookkeeping mistakes

title: The Handover
description: Anthropic's breakout week — first profit, a huge new valuation, and a two-trillion-dollar IPO plan • Nvidia's five-hundred-billion-dollar financing alliance with Wall Street • Google DeepMind's leadership shake-up and a wave of big-lab talent churn • A third AI lab reports its own model breached a real company during safety testing • France's under-fifteen social media ban struck down by its own top court • The largest AI-infrastructure supply-chain breach disclosed so far this year

title: The Pressure Campaign
description: OpenAI pauses its next frontier training run — the aftershock of a safety story we already told you • A genuine catch-up: OpenAI's "Astra" solved ten historically unsolved maths problems three weeks ago, and we missed it • Hedging away from Nvidia — Google's stake in Marvell and Stripe's acquisition of OpenRouter • The AI capex-bubble debate gets a lot louder, including from Jim Cramer • This year's AI-linked layoffs have already passed all of last year's • GitHub's worldwide outage

title: The Promotion Trap
description: - The EU AI Act's extraterritorial compliance rules landed on 2 August — what's actually required, and the callback to the OpenAI compliance story from a few weeks back - The promotion trap — why a great task-based employee can fail at the exact same job once it's a metrics-based one (Accidental MBA) - Three systems for finding the 3 to 6 per cent of a list that's actually ready to buy, right now (Accidental MBA) - Quick mentions: two short Girdley's Letter stories about knowing when a strategy's stopped working, plus three book recommendations

title: Losing Control
description: Running order: 1. Nvidia's extraordinary week — earnings, the Hugging Face deal, and the capex-bubble debate 2. OpenAI's Jalapeño chip posts its first benchmarks against Nvidia 3. Anthropic's big week — Salesforce "Claudeforce" and a thirty-trillion-dollar IPO pitch 4. AI agents in the wild — a real ransomware breach and a hundred-and-sixteen-company defence letter 5. AI investment aggregate — half-year funding hits four hundred and seven billion dollars 6. Meta's teen-addiction settlement finalised at up to eighteen billion dollars 7. Taiwan indicts nine over B300 chip smuggling to China 8. Iran and the Strait of Hormuz — contradictory claims of control 9. Ukraine — deadliest single attack of the war so far 10. UK — Burnham delivers on cost-of-living pledges against a harder economic backdrop 11. Microsoft's "Frontier Accelerate" partner overhaul 12. Quick-fire round — AI, Tech, Geopolitics & UK, Microsoft

title: The Five-Advisor Council
description: - A structured AI prompt for pressure-testing a stuck business decision — five role-played advisors, anonymous peer review between them, then a "Chairman" forced to actually pick a side - What a decades-old milk ad rivalry says about the difference between an audience that notices you and one that buys from you - Quick mentions: a handful of small-business anecdotes pulled from the same newsletter's own link roundup
